newsitem.title: USA: Dow Corning files reorganization plan.
newsitem.headline: Dow Corning files reorganization plan.

text.p: Dow Corning said Monday it filed a plan to emerge from Chapter 11 bankruptcy and settle lawsuits by women with silicone breast implants previously made by the company.

Dow Chemical and Dow Corning Corp., a joint venture with Corning Inc., have been sued by thousands of women who allege the implants have caused medical problems such as connective tissue diseases. The company declared bankruptcy in May 1995.

In the reorganization plan, filed with the U.S. Bankruptcy Court in Bay City, Mich., Dow Corning said its plan provides choices for women with implants on how to resolve their claims with flexible options while preserving their right to a jury trial if they want it.
The Midland, Mich.-based company said the value of breast implant claims should be based on the "best and most compelling scientific evidence available."

As a result, Dow Corning proposed that a court-appointed, independent panel of doctors and scientific experts assess all available studies to determine if there is legitimate and sufficient proof of a connection between silicone breast implants and disease.
A jury should hear testimony from the scientific panel to decide whether claims that breast implants cause disease should be compensated by Dow Corning, it said.

"The plan also provides fair treatment for all women by eliminating any bias in favour of who was first with a court date, who filed in a specific court, or with a specific attorney," said Richard A. Hazleton, chairman and chief executive of Dow Corning.

"The plan demonstrates our commitment to treat everyone with legitimate claims fairly and at the same time preserves the viability of the company, for our customers, employees and others who rely on us."
Dow Chemical's stock fell 62.5 cents to $83.125 and Corning was unchanged at $40.50 early on the New York Stock Exchange.
